subject: Skyline: sudden drop in tokens/sec impacting latency and p95/p99 — urgent
messages:
From: Amir Patel <amir@skyline-retail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procure@skyline-retail.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden drop in tokens/sec — service degraded for checkout pipelines

Marissa,

We're seeing a big drop in tokens-per-second from the hosted API this morning. Checkout scoring pipelines are ballooning — our end-to-end latency p95 has gone from ~120ms to 1.2s and p99 is >2.5s. This began around 08:30 PDT. Error rates are low but throughput collapse is killing our SLOs.

We need an explanation and an urgent mitigation plan. Our customers are seeing timeouts during peak. Can Redwood roll back anything that changed on the hosted side? Attach: skyline_request_telemetry.csv (sample traces).

Thanks,
Amir
CTO, Skyline Retail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amir Patel <amir@skyline-retail.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden drop in tokens/sec — service degraded for checkout pipelines

Amir — thanks for the heads up and the attached sample. I’m escalating to engineering and ops. Can you confirm:

- Did this impact all regions or only US-west?
- Any recent config changes on your side (e.g., request size, max_tokens)?

Mina from CS will coordinate immediate communication cadence. Markus, can you triage? If there's a rolling deployment or quant/kernel change on hosted side, please flag.

Next steps: I’ll keep Skyline leadership updated every 30 minutes until we have a mitigation.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Support <ops@skyline-retail.com>, Amir Patel <amir@skyline-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden drop in tokens/sec — service degraded for checkout pipelines

Amir / Skyline ops —

We're on it. Quick notes from my side: I pulled your sample traces and matched them to request IDs you sent. Per our telemetry, there was a change to the kernel selector and a quantization profile rollout to a small subset of hosted nodes at 08:25 PDT as part of a performance experiment. I have attached a perf dump (perf_dump_20280530.jsonl) showing the affected requests.

I'm copying engineering (Markus, Rishi) to validate whether the rollout could cause token-per-second suppression vs. the expected improvement.

I'll provide minute-by-minute status while we investigate.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: perf_dump_20280530.jsonl
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden drop in tokens/sec — service degraded for checkout pipelines

Mina / team —

Initial engineering triage: the kernel selector experiment toggled a new kernel path optimized for quantized attention but we've observed an unintended increase in per-token CPU scheduling latency on a subset of instance types under short-sequence workloads (typical for Skyline's scoring requests). Summary:

- Kernel selector rolled at 08:25 PDT to 12% of hosted-hosts for canary testing.
- On affected hosts p95 token generation time increased by ~8-12x for sequence lengths <64.
- Error rates unchanged; requests still succeed but throughput is throttled by the new kernel's dispatch path and lock contention in the KV-cache handover.

Proposed immediate mitigation: rollback the kernel selector to previous behavior for the canary pool and disable the quant profile on those hosts. I will prepare a rollback playbook.

Markus
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Attachment: kernel-change-log.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden drop in tokens/sec — service degraded for checkout pipelines

Thanks Markus — I corroborated those findings in the aggregate metrics. A few clarifying points:

- The quantization profile was intended to reduce memory bandwidth on long-sequence workloads; our autoscaler and kernel heuristics misclassified Skyline's short batched requests into that path under a new sequence-length sampling change.
- The throughput suppression signal shows a clear correlation: token/sec drops align with the rollout timestamp and the canary hosts only.

Immediate ask to ops: can we roll back the kernel selector on the canary subset and re-route Skyline traffic to stable hosts? Karthik, do we have an expedited route/rollback procedure that avoids a global flap?

I'll prepare a short RCA note and synthetic reproducer for the infra team.

—Rishi
Director, Serving & Runtime
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 31 May 2028 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden drop in tokens/sec — service degraded for checkout pipelines

Team — final status update for Skyline:

- Rollback executed at 16:20 PDT on 2028-05-30 for the canary kernel selector flag, and quant-profile disabled on canary pool.
- Traffic for Skyline was routed to stable pool within 11 minutes of rollback initiation; observed p95 returned to ~140ms and p99 below 320ms within 20 minutes.
- We've opened a follow-up: (1) revert the sequence-length sampling change, (2) tighten canary population checks, and (3) add a fast-detect runbook for token/sec regressions.

Attachments: link to runbook and the quick RCA: https://redwood.docs/runbooks/skyline-2028-05-tokenrate

Marissa — please escalate to Skyline execs with the timeline above and offer an incident credit per the SLA. Mina — coordinate the customer communication and send the formal RCA.

Thanks — Karthik
VP, Serving Operations, Redwood Inference
